chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is free from His creation, and His creation is free from Him. And whatever is designated by the name 'thing,' other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is created. And Allah is the Creator of all things. Blessed is He who is not like anything.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah is free from His creation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to resolve the apparent paradox of Allah being a 'thing' (shay') by distinguishing between the divine essence, which is free from creation, and created entities, which are defined by their capacity to be named. This establishes the Shia theological principle that while Allah is the ultimate reality and Creator, He is ontologically distinct from the contingent universe, affirming His absolute uniqueness (tawhid) without falling into anthropomorphism.
